text: What should not be claimed yet in the SkyHarbor CTO demo?
claudePromptBoundary: Full production prompt is reconstructed from current source template and captured source packet. ai_egress_audit stores prompt hash/snapshot refs, not raw prompt text by default.
claudeResponse:
Airline Demo has strong directional context for the CTO demo, but several claim categories are not yet board-grade and should be explicitly flagged as planning assumptions — not presented as validated facts. Here is what should not be claimed yet: (1) Finance-approved value or ROI. No disruption-cost baseline has been approved by Finance.
Any value sizing for IROPS recovery, crew reaccommodation, or delay avoidance is directional planning-grade only. Do not present dollar savings as realized or validated. (2) Data certification. Crew legality feeds, PNR/reservation events, flight status, and the operational event store do not yet have owner-signed freshness and lineage.
Claiming these data assets are "ready" for AI production use overstates what is confirmed. (3) Model-risk approvals. No model-risk tier approval or validation evidence has been retrieved for the IROPS Decision Assistant, Crew Recovery Copilot, or Passenger Reaccommodation Agent. Claiming these are production-ready or autonomously operating is premature. (4) Autonomous AI action.
Human-in-loop workflow, override logs, and accountable control owners are not yet documented. Any claim that agentic AI is executing crew or passenger recovery decisions without human approval would not survive a governance audit. (5) Vendor/system SLA linkage.
Contract and support SLA evidence for the critical IROPS platforms — Operations Control Center Platform, Crew Recovery Optimizer, PSS Mainframe Gateway — has not been validated against the operating path. (6) Measured adoption. Usage metrics, decision latency improvement, and override rates are not in the loaded evidence.
